body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #328

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Branch `bb/relay-123-mcp-integration-01-07-store-mcp-server-thr_t6bh922k8p` pushed to origin successfully.

## Summary

Implements issue #123: seeds a Semprec-owned `mcpServers` system database and wires it into the propose/confirm flow so a human can attach credentials without ever exposing them to the AI-authored proposal path.

- **New system database** `mcpServers` (`seedMcpModule.ts`): `name`, `connectionConfig` (strict `stdio`/`sse`/`http`-discriminated JSON schema in `mcp/mcpConnectionConfig.ts`), `active`, plus system-owned `syncStatus`/`lastSynced`. Seeded via a dedicated "MCP" project item, following the existing `seedEmailModule` pattern, wired into `seedSystem.ts`.
- **Proposal validation** (`mcp/mcpServerProposal.ts`, hooked into `assertValidProposalEnvelope`): rejects any credential-shaped field (`credential`, `apiKey`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, etc.) outright, and enforces `connectionConfig` strictness for any proposal targeting `mcpServers`.
- **Credential attachment on confirm** (`proposalActions.ts`): `confirmProposalWithClient` gained an optional `credential` parameter — a human-supplied secret stored via the existing `external_credentials` store in the same transaction as the item creation (atomic: either both persist or neither does), and rejected for any non-`mcpServers` target.
- `syncStatus`/`lastSynced` are `owner: 'system'`, which structurally blocks both the proposal path and any future agent path from touching them or triggering a sync — no MCP-specific sync-blocking code needed (sync itself is out of scope, deferred to issue #125).

**Verification performed this session:**
- New integration suite `mcpServerProposal.test.ts` (12 tests): seed shape, config validation, credential-field rejection, atomic confirm-with-credential, confirm-without-credential, and confirm-refuses-credential-for-wrong-target (with rollback verified).
- Full `pnpm run test` (unit + integration + e2e): 467 integration tests + 5 e2e tests + unit tests, all passing, including the pre-existing `proposalActions.test.ts` regression suite and a required update to `smoke.test.ts`'s exact seeded-database-name list.
- `pnpm -r run build` (all 9 workspace packages) and `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm run check:boundaries` (dependency-cruiser): no violations.

No plaintext credential is ever stored in item properties, proposal history, or logs.

Pushed successfully to branch **`bb/relay-123-mcp-integration-01-07-store-mcp-server-thr_t6bh922k8p`** (`3a18988..7a07f85`).

This push adds the fix for the medium-severity review finding on PR #328: `assertValidMcpServerProposalProperties` now also rejects credential-shaped keys inside a `stdio` transport's `connectionConfig.env` map (normalized to catch `apiKey`, `API_KEY`, `api-key`, etc.), closing the smuggling gap where a secret could bypass the top-level denylist and land in `items.properties` instead of the encrypted `external_credentials` store. Three new tests cover this: rejecting `env.apiKey`, rejecting `env.API_KEY`, and accepting a benign `env.LOG_LEVEL`.

Verified before push: full `pnpm run test` (unit + integration + e2e) passes with exit code 0, `pnpm -r run build` compiles clean across all 11 backend workspace packages, and `pnpm run check:boundaries` reports no dependency violations.

Pushed successfully to branch **`bb/relay-123-mcp-integration-01-07-store-mcp-server-thr_t6bh922k8p`** (`7a07f85..bf84da3`).

This push adds the fix for the latest medium-severity review finding on PR #328: `sse`/`http` transport `connectionConfig.url` query-string parameters were not checked against the credential-field denylist, letting a secret smuggled as a URL query param (e.g. `?token=sk-...`) bypass both the top-level property check and the Zod schema and land in plaintext in `items.properties`. Added `assertNoCredentialShapedUrlParams` (`backend/packages/data/src/mcp/mcpServerProposal.ts`), which parses the URL and checks each query-param name against the same normalized denylist already used for `stdio`'s `env` map, with three new tests covering the rejection, its normalized-case variant, and a benign param passing through untouched.

Verified before push: full `pnpm run test` (unit + integration + e2e) passes with exit code 0, `pnpm -r run build` compiles clean across all 11 backend workspace packages, and `pnpm run check:boundaries` reports no dependency violations.
